For this project, I'm interested in how reported childcare capacity varies across Baltimore ZIP codes. I'll explore the MDPS Early Childhood data to compare program records, program settings, and capacity for different age groups. I'll also check missing information and repeated addresses before interpreting the comparisons.

I want to see how childcare programs and their reported capacity vary across Baltimore ZIP codes. I’m also interested in whether different program settings have different schedules and serve different age groups.

I’m starting by looking through the table, checking what needs cleaning, and trying a few charts. I’m using the course’s EDA notes to help organize the process. At this point, I’m looking for patterns and figuring out which comparisons are actually useful.

1. Inspect the columns and clean the data.
2. Check missing information and possible duplicate records.
3. Summarize childcare capacity by ZIP code.
4. Compare program counts, capacities, and program settings.
5. Write short notes about the patterns in the results.

```{r}
#| label: setup

# Starting by using https://umbc-viz.github.io/ges778/notes/05_eda.html to structure this EDA. First, I’m loading the packages and making a working copy of the data. I’m removing rows without an address so I can focus on the program records.

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)

childcare <- read.csv(file.choose(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#^ I used this to connect to the dataset MDPS Early Childhood Dev.csv. This would allow for reporduction as long as the table was accessible. 

childcare_eda <- childcare |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(address),
    address != ""
  )

# The original table had seven footnote rows at the bottom. Filtering out rows without addresses lets me keep those notes in the original file without including them in the analysis.

dim(childcare_eda)
names(childcare_eda)
head(childcare_eda)
summary(childcare_eda)

# These are quick checks of the table's size, column names, and values. They help me get familiar with the data, but I need to dig deeper before deciding what is worth graphing.
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(childcare_eda))
```


```{r}
#| Label: Histogram_Function

capacity_histogram <- function(variable, bins = 40){ 
  ggplot(childcare_eda, aes(x = {{ variable }}))+
    geom_histogram(
      bins = bins, fill = "navy", color = "white"
    ) + 
    labs(
      x = "Reorted Capacity", y = "Number of Program Records"
    )
}

# Since I want several similar histograms, I'm making a function so I can change the column without rewriting the chart. The bins control how the values are grouped into bars.

capacity_histogram(total_capacity_1) + 
  labs(title = "Total Childcare Capacity")

childcare_eda$Infant.Capacity.. <- as.numeric(
  as.character(childcare_eda$Infant.Capacity..)) 
capacity_histogram(Infant.Capacity.., bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Infant capacity")

# This code was not working properly since it wasn't numeric this was because the data set had footnotes in the bottom 7 rows as next.

capacity_histogram(Center.Toddler.Capacity, bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Toddler capacity")

capacity_histogram(Preschool.Capacity, bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Preschool capacity")

capacity_histogram(School.Age..capacity..., bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "School-age capacity")

# I'm using these to check the spread of capacities and see whether a few large programs stand out from the smaller ones. Missing values are left out of the histograms.
```

```{r}
#| Label: Density_Zip-capacity

# https://umbc-viz.github.io/ges778/extras/summarizing.html

programs_zip <- childcare_eda |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    zipcode %in% c(zipcode),
    !is.na(total_capacity_1),
    total_capacity_1 <= 300
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    zipcode = as.character(zipcode)
  )

# For this chart, I'm keeping capacities of 300 or less this is to cover every program capacity. I used zipcodes as the category since it was the best field to agrigate too. I wouldve prefered to use neighborhoods and if i was to develop further this would be the way. 

# If doing spatial analysis this can be developed further. 

zip_avg <- programs_zip |>
  dplyr::group_by(zipcode) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    capacity_mean = mean(total_capacity_1)
  )

zip_avg

# The product of this gives the average program capacity for each zipcode. These averages can develope a solid comparison of program acessibility over space. 
```

```{r}
#| Label: Density_Zip-capacity_chart

ggplot(
  programs_zip,
  aes(x = total_capacity_1, fill = zipcode)
) + 
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = capacity_mean, color = zipcode),
    data = zip_avg,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of program capacity by ZIP code",
    subtitle = "Vertical lines show mean program capacity",
    x = "Reported capacity per program",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "ZIP code",
    color = "ZIP code"
  )

# This is not usable but has a good example of the data i wish to continue examining. The curves show how program sizes are distributed within each zipcodes, and the vertical lines show the averages.
```

```{r}
#| Label: Capcity_Days-Open

program_day <- childcare_eda |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(total_capacity_1),
    total_capacity_1 <= 300
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      # I made these colums in the excel before bringing into here. The time_days_open column was laid out with each day ex. ["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday"] this seemed unneccisarly difficult to adjust so the other columns were made. 
      Monday.Open,
      Tuesday.Open,
      Wednesday.Open,
      Thursday.Open,
      Friday.Open,
      Saturday.Open,
      Sunday.Open
    ),
    names_to = "day",
    values_to = "open"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(open == "Yes") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = factor(
      day,
      levels = c(
        "Monday.Open",
        "Tuesday.Open",
        "Wednesday.Open",
        "Thursday.Open",
        "Friday.Open",
        "Saturday.Open",
        "Sunday.Open"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Mon",
        "Tue",
        "Wed",
        "Thu",
        "Fri",
        "Sat",
        "Sun"
      )
    )
  )

program_day_avg <- program_day |>
  dplyr::group_by(day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    capacity_mean = mean(total_capacity_1)
  )

program_day_avg

# Before i started the analysis here in R i spent time making columns in the table placing the days in the DAY.Open columns. I marked the days they were open as yes/no based off if they gave a times for when open/closed on that day. 

# While not a chart this is showing a curve that drops during the skews sligly in the middle of the week then drops off during the weekend. 
```

```{r}
#| Label: Capcity_Days-Open_Chart

ggplot(
  program_day,
  aes(x = total_capacity_1, fill = day)
) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = capacity_mean, color = day),
    data = program_day_avg,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Program capacity by day open",
    subtitle = "Programs with capacity of 200 or less, lines show the means",
    x = "Reported capacity per program",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Day open",
    color = "Day open"
  )

# This chart compares the sizes of childcare programs open on each day. The x-axis shows reported capacity, the colors represent different days, and the vertical lines show each day’s average program capacity. Its use case seems limited as the data is so clustered the visualization isnt great. 

# Density shows where program sizes are concentrated. Using the capacity we can find the averages for each day.

# The curves here are the percentage of programs capacity on the different days. The massive spike shows that on saturday has 47% of its programs with a capacity of 5-10 spaces. 

```

```{r}
#| label: heatmap_program-avaibility-setup

availability <- childcare_eda |>
  select(
    setting = gen_program_setting_detail,
    ends_with(".Time")
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with(".Time"),
    names_to = c("day", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)\\.(Start|End)\\.Time"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    opening = as.numeric(as.difftime(trimws(Start), units = "hours")),
    closing = as.numeric(as.difftime(trimws(End), units = "hours")),
    day = factor(day, levels = day_order)
  ) |>
  # Here i needed to do some work since the times needed to be turned into numbers. The listed 6:30 has now become 6.5 for this analysis. 
  
  tidyr::drop_na(opening, closing) |>
   # We had to add this to drop the days without usable times instead of counting them as closed. The dataset had 44 days with opening times but no closing time that is what we are dropping here.
  
  tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "hour") |>
  mutate(
    hour = hour - 1,
    open = ifelse(
      closing < opening,
      hour >= opening | hour < closing,
      hour >= opening & hour < closing
    )
  ) |>
  # Making 24 rows for each program-day, one for each hour. We do hour -1 to since we have 0 listed that'll list out 24 hours. I'm checking whether the program is open at the start of each hour, including schedules that go past midnight.
  
  group_by(setting, day, hour) |>
  summarise(
    percent_open = mean(open) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Using the grouped-mean approach TRUE counts as 1 and FALSE as 0, so their average times 100 gives the percentage open. This lets us throw the values into a heatmap.
  
  tidyr::complete(setting, day, hour = 0:23)
```

```{r}
#| label: heatmap_program-avaibility
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 11

ggplot(
  availability,
  aes(x = hour, y = day, fill = percent_open)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(
  ~ setting,
  ncol = 1,
  strip.position = "top"
) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 23, 2),
    expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = rev(day_order),
    labels = rev(c(
      "Mon", 
      "Tue", 
      "Wed", 
      "Thu", 
      "Fri", 
      "Sat", 
      "Sun")
      ),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "grey95",
    high = "navy",
    limits = c(0, 100),
    na.value = "grey95"
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly Childcare Availability",
    subtitle = "By MDPS program setting",
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Open Programs Precentage",
    caption = paste0(
      "Only program-days with usable opening and closing times are included.\n",
      "Grey represents both unschedule information and times.\n",
      "Source: MDPS Early Childhood dataset (2026)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0,
      size = 12),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 20,
      color = "navy"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      margin = margin(b = 35)
    ),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1, 1.06),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```
